body:
I think defaulting one type variable to another one is what causes the problem. If I try `default=int` everything works.
cc @JelleZijlstra @cdce8p who worked on defaults a while ago.

> I think defaulting one type variable to another one is what causes the problem.

Not completely. Yes, it's one of the few areas where the Mypy implementation of PEP 696 is still incomplete. However, basic examples should work. This looks like an error in the deferral logic. Just moving `Alias` after `MyClass` does resolve it.

```py
from typing import Generic, TypeVar, TypeAlias

T1 = TypeVar("T1")
T2 = TypeVar("T2", default=T1)

class MyClass(Generic[T1, T2]): ...

Alias: TypeAlias = "MyClass[T1, T2]"
```

Just saw that by only removing the explicit `TypeAlias` annotation, the crash goes away as well.
```diff
 from typing import Generic, TypeVar, TypeAlias
 
 T1 = TypeVar("T1")
 T2 = TypeVar("T2", default=T1)
 
-Alias: TypeAlias = "MyClass[T1, T2]"
+Alias = "MyClass[T1, T2]"
 
 class MyClass(Generic["T1", "T2"]): ...
```

> Just saw that by only removing the explicit `TypeAlias` annotation, the crash goes away as well.
> 
>  from typing import Generic, TypeVar, TypeAlias
>  
>  T1 = TypeVar("T1")
>  T2 = TypeVar("T2", default=T1)
>  
> -Alias: TypeAlias = "MyClass[T1, T2]"
> +Alias = "MyClass[T1, T2]"
>  
>  class MyClass(Generic["T1", "T2"]): ...

Unfortunately, without `: TypeAlias` it won't be usable as a type alias, as it's just a plain string.

Removing annotation makes it a string LOL. Anyway, what I want to say is that it is not a problem with deferral in general, it either doesn't handle type var defaults correctly or vice-versa defaults don't handle deferral correctly.

The following causes namespace drift, so the alias appears as changed on every iteration:

https://github.com/python/mypy/blob/68233f6ff328f35c7ac26a7efdd325ae1248468b/mypy/tvar_scope.py#L109

`TypeVarLikeNamespaceSetter` modifies **in-place**. Stepping through in pdb, every iteration appears as "changed" here:

https://github.com/python/mypy/blob/68233f6ff328f35c7ac26a7efdd325ae1248468b/mypy/semanal.py#L4110

```
(Pdb) existing.node.target.args[0].id.namespace, res.args[0].id.namespace
('a.MyClass', 'a.Alias')
```

issue.title: Type variable defaults, solved for partially-parameterised generic types, do not reset
issue.body:
**Bug Report, To Reproduce, & Actual Behaviour**

See [mypy Playground](https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=master&python=3.12&gist=853adf145cd601e0761eaa16481f2db3):

```python
from typing_extensions import Generic, TypeVar

T1 = TypeVar("T1")
T2 = TypeVar("T2", default=T1)

class MyClass(Generic[T1, T2]): ...

reveal_type(MyClass[int])  # N: Revealed type is "def [T2 = builtins.int] () -> __main__.MyClass[builtins.int, T2`2 = builtins.int]"

# `T2` now defaults to `int` for `MyClass` from now on
reveal_type(MyClass[str])  # N: Revealed type is "def [T2 = builtins.int] () -> __main__.MyClass[builtins.str, T2`2 = builtins.int]"
reveal_type(MyClass[bytes])  # N: Revealed type is "def [T2 = builtins.int] () -> __main__.MyClass[builtins.bytes, T2`2 = builtins.int]"
```

**Expected Behavior**

```python
reveal_type(MyClass[str])  # N: Revealed type is "def [T2 = builtins.str] () -> __main__.MyClass[builtins.str, T2`2 = builtins.str]"
reveal_type(MyClass[bytes])  # N: Revealed type is "def [T2 = builtins.bytes] () -> __main__.MyClass[builtins.bytes, T2`2 = builtins.bytes]"
```

**Your Environment**

- Mypy version used: 1.15, 1.16
- Mypy command-line flags: None
- Mypy configuration options from `mypy.ini` (and other config files): None
- Python version used: 3.9, 3.12

issue.title: Fix crashes caused by typevarlikes defaults in-place modifications
issue.body:
Fixes #19185. Fixes #19186.

Replaces #19382 (not closing that yet, need to extract another part related to `applytype` from there to another PR).

When a `TypeVar` defaults to another `TypeVar`, that default should already be in scope. Fortunately we already analyze them in the correct order, so the active scope has all the necessary information. This fixes the namespace drift problem because the bound typevars are already adjusted to use the correct namespace, and we do not need to touch their global definitions.

I am not super happy about making TypeVarLikeScope impure here - any suggestions? Would passing `self.msg` to every `bind_new` call look saner?
